diagnosis.summary: Checkout‑api latency spiked after the 10:15 deployment, with p95 rising from 200 ms to over 2 s. The spike was caused by a reduced database connection pool that exhausted connections during checkout requests.
diagnosis.root_cause: The new config set orders‑db pool max_connections to 10 and acquire_timeout_ms to 2000 ms, causing ConnectionPoolTimeoutError and long db.pool.acquire spans.

evidence.finding: Diff shows pool.max_connections changed from 50 to 10 and acquire_timeout_ms set to 2000 ms.
p95 latency jumped from 200 ms pre‑deploy to 2150 ms post‑deploy within minutes.
212 ERROR logs of ConnectionPoolTimeoutError with waiting=143 and acquire_timeout_ms=2000 ms in last 15 min.
db.pool.acquire span lasted 1829 ms, dominating the 2142 ms request.
in_use=10, waiting=143, acquire_wait_p95_ms=1800 ms, exceeding baseline max_connections of 50.

ruled_out: External service outage – payment-gateway.authorize completed in 187 ms.
Network partition – no related logs and latency only after deployment.
Staging‑to‑prod drift – staging on v4.17 runs without exhaustion due to lower traffic.

proposal.rationale: The latency spike is caused by a reduced orders‑db connection pool in the new release (v4.17). Rolling back to the previous stable release (v4.16) restores the original pool settings and eliminates ConnectionPoolTimeoutError spikes, restoring normal p95 latency.
